subject: Charter shuttle + last-mile transport — cost split & security for TruHealth onsite
messages:
From: Bryan Cole <bryan@truhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Onsite logistics: exec arrivals and last-mile transport

Hi Stephanie,

Appreciate you coordinating — our leadership team will be onsite in SF for the TruHealth/Redwood workshop on Oct 21. We have a tight arrival window: four senior attendees arriving between 10:30–11:05 AM at SFO and one arriving on a later redeye. Given the security sensitivity and tight schedule, our office has asked whether Redwood can arrange a private shuttle/charter from the airport to the TruHealth campus (approx 45 mins) and back for departures.

Key asks from our side:
- Secure, unmarked vehicles with privacy screens for our execs (no open signage).
- A staggered pickup window and a guaranteed last-mile drop at TruHealth HQ.
- Vendor must provide certificate of insurance and driver background check confirmation.

I know this is outside standard travel policy — happy to share cost if needed. Do you have a preferred vendor or should we put you in touch with the event logistics company we use (GlobalEventCo)?

Thanks,
Bryan Cole
CTO, TruHealth Inc
bryan@truhealth.com
(415) 555-0198

Date: 2026-10-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Onsite logistics: exec arrivals and last-mile transport

Team — forwarding Bryan's note. Quick summary and ask:

Situation:
- TruHealth execs (4 arriving mid-morning, 1 late) requesting a private shuttle/charter SFO -> TruHealth HQ for Oct 21 due to security and timing.
- Vendor suggested: GlobalEventCo (external).

What I need from each of you:
- Monica: vendor quote + insurance and lead-time check so we know whether 72h is sufficient. Please confirm vehicle types and pickup windows.
- Marcus: guidance on whether we can absorb the expense under Corporate Events and whether a one-time policy exception is required for a charter (estimate > $5k). If so, what approval path / cap do you need?
- Laura: advise on whether we should cover 60% of the shuttle as a customer concession or ask TruHealth to split 50/50 — your call for sales optics.
- David: executive sign-off if we need policy exception for chartering or heightened local security.

Bryan indicated they're willing to cost-share; I suggested Redwood lead the booking to ensure vendor meets our insurance/security requirements and then invoice TruHealth per agreed split.

I've cc'd no external vendors yet — want to get internal greenlight before engaging.

Thanks — can we aim to confirm by EOD so I can hold vendor availability?

— Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie — I've reached out to GlobalEventCo; they're available but need confirmation quickly. Attached: globalevents_quote_8721.pdf (detailed line items) and insurance_cert_globalevents.pdf (vendor COI). Highlights from quote:

- 2x 12-passenger black SUVs (privacy glass) + 1x 20-person mini-coach for baggage and close protection escort.
- Total base cost (vehicle + drivers + wait time): $6,800.
- Add-on: driver background summary & amber-shield screening = $450.
- Cancellation: full refund if canceled >72 hours; 50% if within 72 hours.

Vendor notes: they need a PO or deposit to lock vehicles; 72-hour lead time is firm for vehicle allocation. They require a W9 and banking info before invoicing; insurance cert included.

Action items for booking: provide charge code / GL, confirm how much Redwood will cover (percent), and whether we proceed with the driver screening add-on (recommended for execs).

Attaching the vendor docs now.

— Monica Patel
Events Ops Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick finance checklist before I can approve:

1) Need line-item cost breakdown by vehicle (quote has that, good). Please confirm per-head equivalent and final total including the driver screening add-on.
2) We will treat this as Corporate Events expense. For a charter > $5,000 we require an explicit one-time exception logged in Concur and a PO. I can approve an exception up to $7,500 from Corporate Events but need: vendor W9, banking info, and confirmation of how costs will be split with TruHealth (if any).
3) Please provide the GL / charge code. If sales wants to subsidize, we need the internal cost split (e.g., Redwood 65% / TruHealth 35%) to be recorded on the PO.

If you can get vendor W9 and confirm split, I'll issue approval and instruct procurement to raise the PO.

- Marcus Lin
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

All — I'm comfortable approving a one-time policy exception to secure a charter for TruHealth's senior leadership, subject to the following conditions:

- Cap the Redwood portion at $7,500 total. If final total exceeds that, Laura/sales to push for a higher TruHealth contribution.
- Vendor must provide W9 and primary banking info (for procurement).
- Include the driver screening add-on; no compromise on background checks.
- Monica to confirm pickup windows and an alternate plan if traffic causes >20 min delay (fallback: expedited follow-up vehicle).

Marcus — please mark the Concur exception and proceed with PO issuance once W9 is in hand. Laura — if Redwood covers >60%, make sure Sales is comfortable with the optics; prefer Redwood = 65% / TruHealth = 35% if we can absorb the security delta.

Proceed once the vendor paperwork is complete.

-David

- Laura: confirm sales ok with 65% concession (please reply here).
